reason:
The headline is false, and I disproved it by driving the exact experiment the seat should have run. Driven at ?v=light&state=error, 1440x960, reducedMotion, I re-inserted the verbatim r1 defect line that this assertion was written to guard - the one deleted by panel/fix-r1-batch3.py:39, `

Last good reading · ${esc(D.readingLong)}

` - into `main .center`. `claimsLastGood` went false -> TRUE and the predicate `!claimsLastGood` evaluated FALSE. The assertion fails on reintroduction of the defect it names. It is a narrow literal-phrase regression guard, not a vacuous assertion. The seat's reasoning - 'the string appears nowhere in lately.html or fixture.js, it therefore cannot fail' - is a logic error: 'cannot fail' means no reachable input falsifies it, not 'does not fail on today's source'. Every negative regression assertion in this file is absent from the fixed source by construction; the seat's test would condemn all of them. That distinction is exactly what separates this from the four genuinely vacuous assertions the round notes count. SUB-CLAIM 2 IS FACTUALLY TRUE AND WRONG AS A CRITICISM. The scoping is deliberate and must stay. `main` is a sibling of `header.top` (lately.html:933-949; driven, `header.parentElement` is the shell DIV, `main.querySelector('header')` is null), so the assertion by design does not see the header stamp - because the header stamp is SANCTIONED. interaction-check.mjs:351-361 requires `anchored >= 1` for state=error, and r1's own adjudication (panel/round-1/refuters/error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading.json, sharpenedFix clause 3) ruled that the header's 'Read at' and the coverage strip's 'Read' must be treated as one decision and not dropped. The r1 defect was the label INSIDE the error card, which is inside `main`. An assertion that 'looked where the stamp is' would be asserting against a fact the surface is required to print. SUB-CLAIM 3 IS TRUE AND IS THE ONLY LIVE PART. `instances` is computed and spent only on the detail string. Driven with the seat's own paraphrase injection, `instances` goes 0 -> 1 while `claimsLastGood` stays false and the check passes - so a re-stamped instant under any other wording slips the guard. That is a narrow guard, worth one token to widen, not an assertion that cannot fail. THE FIX IS WRONG AND WOULD MAKE THE GATE UNSATISFIABLE. Its headline clause - 'measured over the whole document rather than `main`' - contradicts its own next sentence, which scopes every new predicate back to `main`. Taken literally it asserts `readingLong` appears nowhere in the document; driven, `readingLong` occurs TWICE in the error document (header:944 'Read at', coverage:954 'Read'), both mandatory. That check and 'the reading instant is stated, once - error' could never both be green. Deleting the `Last good reading` regex, as the fix instructs, also discards the one predicate proven to catch a verbatim regression, trading a working guard for a proxy. 'No digit at all in `main`' is currently true (driven: mainText is digit-free) but is a copy rule masquerading as a fabrication rule - it would fire on honest future wording and would not fire on a fabricated magnitude spelled in words. SEVERITY IS OVERSTATED BY A CLASS. Nothing on the artifact is visibly wrong; the guarded defect is closed and stays closed under verbatim regression. The residual - a phrase-grep a paraphrase evades - is a refinement to the gate's strength, which is a reason to refute the finding as filed.
sharpenedFix: Keep the `Last good reading` regex; it is the only predicate proven to fail on a verbatim regression, and deleting it is a strict loss. Keep the `main` scope; the header and coverage stamps are required by interaction-check.mjs:351-361 and by r1's adjudication, and widening to the document makes the gate unsatisfiable. Make one change: fold the already-computed count into the predicate, so the guard states the policy positively rather than grepping one phrase. At interaction-check.mjs:1014, `ok("the error state claims no reading it does not hold", !err.claimsLastGood && err.instances === 0, `${err.instances} stamps`)`. That is the whole fix - it catches the seat's own paraphrase injection (instances 0 -> 1) and every other re-stamp of the reading instant inside the error card, under any label, while leaving the sanctioned header and coverage stamps untouched. Optionally extend `err` to count `readingShort` in `main` the same way and add `&& err.shortInstances === 0`; do not add the open count 9 or the last-four total 31, which are bare integers that will collide with unrelated copy. Do NOT add a 'no digit at all in main' rule. Before landing, break it as the seat says: inject `Last reading: 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026` into `main .center`, confirm the assertion now FAILS where today it passes, then restore and confirm all 461 assertions green.
breaks: The fix as filed breaks the behaviour gate outright: its 'whole document' clause is mutually unsatisfiable with 'the reading instant is stated, once - error' (interaction-check.mjs:351-361, requires anchored >= 1 in state=error, driven count is 2), so interaction-check.mjs could never exit green again, and it would reopen r1's error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading by implying the header stamp is the fabrication. Its 'no digit in main' clause is brittle against any future error-card copy carrying a legitimate number and is a proxy, not the policy. The sharpened one-line change breaks nothing on the surface - it touches only the gate's predicate, not lately.html - but after it lands re-measure: (1) the full interaction-check.mjs run green at all 461 assertions, in particular that `instances === 0` does not fire in state=error today (driven: it is 0); (2) 'the reading instant is stated, once - error' still passes at 2 occurrences; (3) audit.mjs unaffected, since no markup, token, weight or contrast changes.
